title: Visualisations
headline: The winged zebrafish has wings. Panels B, D and E of Compare now draw the parametric designs (winged-zebrafish.glb, wingless-flying-fish.glb, tff.glb) instead of a stand-in body, because a silent refusal to draw reads as a bug and a labelled assumption does not. The honesty moved into the label: each readout gives the pectoral/SL the panel is DRAWN at, the evidence grade of that number, and the delta's own reason from the design's manifest. Panel B says 0.350, assumed delta, not a measured value, a chosen point between the zebrafish placeholder 0.155 and the flying-fish median 0.687 - and still says that the real germline kcnh2a lof/+ ; lat4a nr21/+ double heterozygote exists but that its paired-fin measurements appear ONLY in that paper's figure panels, with nothing digitised, so no fin-ratio value is asserted. Panel D's 0.140 is measured in halfbeaks and hypothetical on a flying fish's body. All four designs (including the 50:50 blend) are also in the species menu under HYPOTHETICAL designs, where the opening panel lays out ancestry, every moved parameter with its delta, reason and evidence grade, the lean_recheck the page has NOT run, and the mesh-derived quantities; every piece's panel repeats that it belongs to a design, not to an observed animal. NEW: a Genotype browser (?mode=genotype) comparing genotype differences across organisms, on the sequences thread's committed files. It leads with the site that separates: lat4a F326L is L in 8 of 9 flying fishes and in both gliding halfbeaks, F in all 24 non-gliding beloniform relatives, and F in every bat, colugo, sugar glider, squirrel, gecko, lizard, snake, frog, mouse and human that was searched. Pick any of the 9 genes and any of its 16 marked variant sites, filter the 52 organisms by role (gliders and fliers, non-gliding controls, the beloniform series), and read the residue each organism carries at each site straight out of the alignment column; set a residue and the organisms sharing that state light up with a count. The beloniform ladder is drawn with the measured fin ratio per group beside the derived-state count, carrying the file's own warning that it is slightly INVERTED (gliding halfbeaks at fin/SL 0.27 carry about as many derived states as flying fishes at 0.69) and that the non-gliders score zero by construction. The glider comparison says 11 shared columns against 17 for the role-swapped baseline, so the baseline scores higher. The orthologue table shows the 7 clean reciprocal best hits and draws the 2 FAILURES (kcnh2a to kcnh7a, shha to shhb) in red as NOT orthologue calls. Every view carries the gene-set caveat: the nine genes were chosen from zebrafish fin biology, so absence of convergence in them says nothing about the rest of the genome. GENOME-LEVEL DESIGN FREEDOM, within what the data support: the browser lets the user set the residue at a marked site and see who shares it, and compose a design as parents-plus-deltas in anatomy-model/parametric's own schema (weights between the two parents, a delta on pectoral_len_over_SL, both parents' values and the composed value side by side, and the record emitted as JSON for that thread's build.py). What it refuses to do is predict: setting a residue changes the comparison and the provenance and nothing else, no mesh is built from a composed record, and the page says in both places that only a CALIBRATED intervention moves the mesh, in the Design Studio. Sequences is no longer a stand-in and no longer throws. sequences/ landed mid-session in a different shape from the one seq.js read (alignments keyed by species rather than listed, the identity matrix nested as an object, variants carrying ref/alt and an alignment column), which made the view crash on load; seq.js now reads both shapes. The alignment tab draws the real per-gene alignments (slc43a2a: 52 species rows including Hirundichthys speculiger and the Beloniformes series, no bird row), the identity tab draws the file's own percentages rather than recomputing them, and the gene list comes from sequences/genes.json. genome-regions.json and engineered-diff.json are in the build but not in a shape this view reads, so their tabs stay empty and the panel names the file and its top-level keys rather than filling them with a stand-in. The Design Studio now runs both ways. It already read phenotype to genotype (change the body, see candidate routes); it now also reads genotype to phenotype, in a Genotype panel that annotates while you design and lets you edit at the genotype level. ANNOTATIONS, per gene: the sequence layer from genotype/sequence-layer.json (7 clean reciprocal-best-hit orthologues in the annotated flying-fish gene set, each with its percent identity and the sentence that presence is not place or time of action; and the 2 labelled FAILURES, kcnh2a and shha, which pair back to kcnh7a and shhb and are drawn in red as NOT an orthologue call, never as one); pathway membership from a build-time slice of genotype/pathways.slim.json (41 genes, 496 pathways, written to blueprint3d/pathways.json) with each pathway's source and evidence codes, the count of electronic (IEA/IBA) rows, and the statement that every Reactome zebrafish row is inferred by orthology from human; the causal chain with its chain strength, strongest rung and named weakest link; the gene's pleiotropy across the map; and its interactions from genotype/interactions.json. EDITING: pick any of the 92 interventions and apply it. Only the 12 flagged usable_as_a_calibrated_knob carry a magnitude, and only inside the regime they were measured in: the one adult-regime knob this Studio has a parameter for (gja1b stp^tl28d, fin ray length ~95 % of wild type 'in both larvae and adults') moves the pectoral fin length to 0.653 SL, the mesh changes and browser-check.mjs re-checks live, which flips C9 from holds to violated and lights the fin red. An embryonic-fin-bud knob (hhip, +65 % fin area at 72-96 hpf) is NOT applied to the adult design, because the two regimes do not interpolate; the row says so and hands it to Growth at 72-96 hpf with one click. Every other intervention can be selected and read in full and moves nothing, saying 'no magnitude reported' and showing the paper's own words. Lethality is shown from the record's own sentence, and a record that says the animals are viable is never drawn as a death warning ('not embryonic lethal' contains the word lethal): 7 of the 11 records that say anything about survival report death, and applying one (ezh2, 'they die at 48 hpf') says the organism would not reach the stage being drawn. Paralog guards are shown on the applied row (no tbx5 route exists at all, and evidence is never moved between paralogues). Applying two interventions never sums them: the panel says no source combines them, each row is read on its own, the model carries at most one magnitude, and the kcnh2a/lat4a double heterozygote is named as the one real double-mutant experiment in the file, with its own compound level. The panel's banner says applying a measured effect is a LOOKUP of one published experiment, not a prediction for this design, and the same-species / cross-species chip from the species switch is on every row. Deep link: ?mode=design&geno=<intervention id>[,<id>]. Open the fish now opens three segmented models, not one: the flying fish (default, unchanged), the adult zebrafish (model/zebrafish-adult.glb, 189 pieces) and the zebrafish larva at ~4-5 dpf (model/zebrafish-larva.glb, 58 pieces), from a species menu and a deep link (?model=flying-fish|zebrafish-adult|zebrafish-larva). Only the selected model is fetched, with a spinner while it loads; switching disposes the old model's geometry and keeps the mode, and every existing deep link still means what it meant. Split, peel, isolate, drill, labels, the camera fit, the gene lens, Physiology, Tissue, Cell, Growth, Sequences and the Design Studio all run on whichever model is selected. The provenance panel was Uberon-only, so every ZFA piece would have missed: each zebrafish piece is now looked up by the manifest's Uberon cross-reference (never by its ZFA id), and where the blueprint has no such class the panel says "no node in the blueprint for <label>" by name and explains that the term exists but this blueprint, read out of a flying-fish description, does not contain it (adult 41 of 189 resolve, 148 do not; larva 16 of 58 resolve, 42 do not). Each piece's trace shows its ZFA id and Uberon xref as OBO links, its organ system (naming the deliberate nulls: fins, swim bladder, notochord and yolk have no ZFA part_of link to a system, and the manifest stores null plus a note rather than a guess), its geometry basis split into sourced clauses (each with the paper's citation and a verbatim quote from anatomy-model/zebrafish/sources.json, copied in by the build) and schematic clauses, and the manifest's note, with the three mappings that are broader than the mesh flagged as such (adult myomeres to myotome, procurrent rays to caudal fin lepidotrichium, larval swim bladder to posterior chamber). lean/morphology-grounding.json was computed on the flying-fish manifest, so it is read only for the flying fish: a zebrafish piece says plainly that no theorem is evaluated against it, instead of inheriting a verdict from a same-named flying-fish piece. Compare's zebrafish panels are no longer the flying-fish body: panels A and B draw the real zebrafish models and swap larva for adult at the boundary the development data defines (Parichy 2009 milestone J, SL 11.0 mm), while C, D and E always hold the flying fish whatever the species menu shows. The honesty text is unchanged and now matches the geometry: the zebrafish fins are drawn as the model has them, at the manifest's schematic 0.19 SL, and are never scaled by a fin ratio, because no sourced wild-type zebrafish pectoral-fin-length / SL exists (development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs returns null); the readout still says "no sourced value", and panel B is drawn exactly like panel A because the "overgrown" fins have no sourced magnitude to draw. The shared camera now pulls in so the largest fish of the moment fills its frame (relative sizes unchanged), which makes the larval ages readable. genotype/interventions.json was measured in zebrafish, so the Design Studio now says what that is worth for the model on screen: with a zebrafish selected the routes are same-species evidence (91 of 92 entries in Danio rerio, each row chipped "same species", the rest "not Danio rerio"), with the flying fish selected they keep the existing cross-species label, each row chipped "cross-species", and the banner and panel both state which it is. The Studio's parameters, baselines and constraint rows stay the flying fish's measured reference and are explicitly NOT applied to zebrafish geometry (the drag handles are hidden and the panel says so), so nothing invents a zebrafish design. Open the fish now runs on every other thread's real files, with no page-side stand-in where a file exists. The Design Studio checks each edit with the Lean thread's browser-check.mjs (copied by the build; the C9 stand-in is gone): rows show holds / violated / cannot-evaluate with the missing input named, red and amber glow on the pieces the grounding links to each theorem, no glow for the unconstrained-inputs row or for inputs no single design can supply, and the banner carries the kernel sentence once (evaluates the same formulas; not a kernel check). The reference is Park and Choi's L3 specimen (SL 0.203 m, 0.06 kg), so the measured fish holds C9 at 10 m/s and every other row names what it lacks. The Studio and Growth list conditions/baseline.json as 'Conditions (locked at average)'; the hypothetical flier from physics/flier/spec.json is a saved design (?mode=design&saved=flier: lifting area 0.04905 m², span 0.664 m, muscle 0.16, 0.06 kg) under a red HYPOTHETICAL banner with the note that climb is power-limited only until the O2 chain is applied (C16 holds at 1 m/s with the bat-derived muscle power; C14 cannot evaluate: no cardiac output or arterial O2). Candidate genetic routes now come from genotype/interventions.json (92 entries): grouped by level (the kcnh2a/lat4a double heterozygote as its own compound level), with grade, chain strength, lesion, stage regime, sources and quotes, pleiotropy and lethality; only calibrated knobs carry a magnitude and none is interpolated; a pectoral fin length edit shows that no calibrated route exists (with the no_sourced_genetic_route notes) and points to hhip loss under fin area (+65 % area at 72 hpf), which can be applied in Growth only inside its measured window, placed on the flying-fish clock by stage progress; paralog guards are shown (no tbx5 route). Growth runs on development/trajectory.mjs (describe() basis lines in the panel, mixed species flagged, proxy/assumed span shaded, derived v_min against the fixed 10 m/s line with the statement that 'first glide' at hatching is an artefact and no sourced size at first glide exists). Tissue and cell views draw genotype/interactions.json's final shape (30 arrows, signal{ligands,receptors,channels,pathway}, inferred_from), lead the tissue view with Braunstein 2021's basal epidermis shha to pre-osteoblast ptch2/smo arrow, draw the 7 ids outside the fin subtree with an 'outside subtree' marker instead of dropping them, and show the 6 refutations as crossed-out 'not established in zebrafish' arrows with their verbatim quotes. Physiology reads gills.json's {value, unit} kPa parameters and circulation.json (28 stations, 38 vessels; vessels with no model piece at named proxy positions, unsourced shares split evenly). New: Compare (?mode=compare), a synced 2x2 of zebrafish / winged zebrafish / flying fish / wingless flying fish plus the TFF with an altitude readout, on development/zebrafish compareAt with the clock-matching axis shown; zebrafish fins are not drawn because no sourced zebrafish pectoral/SL exists. New: Sequences (?mode=sequences), alignment, % identity heatmaps, genome-region track and engineered-vs-divergence bars, on a hatched STAND-IN LAYOUT until sequences/ lands. Open the fish (/blueprint3d/) runs on the other threads' real files where they exist: the gill lamella uses physiology/countercurrent.js (utilisation 56 % counter-current vs 40 % co-current on the stand-in parameters, effectiveness 71 % vs 50 %), the circulation particles beat at the heart rate of physiology/cardiac.js's proxy (schoolmaster snapper, 96 to 153 /min via an effort slider), and every piece's panel opens with the Lean grounding verdict from lean/morphology-grounding.json (pectoral fin: lifting area needed 0.012316 m² at 10 m/s against 0.012688 m² measured). genotype/interactions.json exists but holds no interaction yet, and the tissue and cell views say so with the file's own note. The Physics stage embeds the physics thread's flight simulator. Open the fish (/blueprint3d/) now has four modes: Anatomy (the 3D cutaway), Physiology (animated single-circuit blood flow over the model's organ centres, particles coloured by oxygenation, plus a gill-lamella zoom with water and blood flowing opposite ways, live PO2 profiles and a co-current toggle: counter-current extracts 57 % of the water's O2 and lets blood leave at 116 mmHg against 40 % and 90 mmHg co-current, on stand-in parameters), Tissue signalling and Cell-cell interactions (the fin's tissues, bud parts and post-composed cell types drawn as nodes; arrows styled solid for experimental and dashed for orthology-inferred evidence). Both physiology and interactions run on labelled stand-ins: physiology/ and genotype/interactions.json do not exist yet, every animation states on screen which values are flying-fish data (none), proxy-teleost or assumed, and the build copies the real files in when they land. 'Open the fish' at /blueprint3d/ is now a real 3D cutaway: the Blender-built segmented model (model/flying-fish.glb, 110 named pieces, driven by model/manifest.json) loads in three.js; a split slider swings the L/R halves apart, a peel slider hides skin, then muscle, then skeleton, leaving the organs; clicking any piece opens its ontology node (or says the blueprint has none and names the nearest ancestor) with the gene strip, the drill-down list, and a provenance panel that traces the term and query, explicit claim-graph edges, the Lean constraints that apply with their proof scope (C6 for every node; C8, C8c, C9, C12 for skeleton and fin, all marked as about the model, not the fish), the unsigned nanopub drafts that cite it, and the physics figures for the fin; the gene lens tints every piece a gene touches; the Wing genes preset and the Daane 2021 inset are kept. Only the pectoral fin length (0.687 of standard length) is evidence-backed; the canvas says the geometry is schematic. 'Open the fish' is now the default blueprint page at /blueprint3d/ (approved by Amit 2026-10-31; the radial 3D view stays at /blueprint3d/?view=radial): the genotype-phenotype map as a flying fish opened layer by layer: a schematic side view (drawn for the page, not anatomy), an explode slider for the 13 organ systems, organs fanning from a system, an x-ray of one organ with its tissues and cell-type chips, a ranked gene strip at every level (sufficient > required > expressed, proxy fish only), a gene lens that lights every node a gene touches (3119 genes), and a Wing genes preset that pins kcnk5b, kcnh2a and slc43a2a at the whole pectoral fin, draws the genotype thread's zebrafish fin subtree below it (50 ZFA terms, 5 zebrafish-only, precursor bud on a separate develops_from lane) and states that no wing gene has a record below the organ.  The flying-fish blueprint is drawn in 3D at /blueprint3d/ with its genes: 536 distinct ontology terms (13 organ systems, 67 organs, 198 tissues, 257 cell types), 674 part_of edges, and one gene marker on each of the 79 nodes that has a direct proxy-fish record in the vetted genotype map (genotype/map.vetted.slim.json, a committed source, so a clean checkout reproduces the page) (body 1/1, organ systems 8/13, organs 28/67, tissues 29/198, cell types 14/257); every gene section says the records were measured in zebrafish or medaka, never in a flying fish, and that a node with no record is unstudied, not gene-free. Each node also shows its term, the SPARQL query that produced it, and the kernel-checked structural certificate that covers it beside the biological Lean statement it does not have (0 of 536 terms appear in any Lean statement). /graph/ hides its 213 datasets by default and its Ideas view reads 12 ideas: 4 researched, 5 reach-synthesis (not yet checked against prior art), 3 serendipitous.

needs.ask: run node dashboard/build-graph.mjs before each deploy

if the zebrafish manifests or anatomy-model/zebrafish/sources.json change, rerun node dashboard/build-graph.mjs: it copies manifest-adult.json, manifest-larva.json and sources.json (as model/zebrafish-sources.json) into dashboard/public/blueprint3d/model/. The .glb files are committed there directly and are not copied.

genome-regions.json and engineered-diff.json are keyed by topic (flying_fish, bats / winged_zebrafish, hypothetical_flier) rather than as rows. Either add a rows[] with {locus, kind, source} and {label, value, kind}, or tell the viz thread which keys to read and it will adapt seq.js.

the genotype browser reads alignments/*.json, gliders.json and progression.json. If the alignment shape changes (alignment keyed by species, percent_identity nested, variants carrying alignment_column_1based), tell the viz thread: seq.js reads both the old and the new shape today.

next: Genotype browser: the composer blends only the two parents the 50:50 chimera manifest carries (flying fish, zebrafish adult), because that is the only committed file holding both parents' value for every parameter. A parent table published by anatomy-model/parametric would let any organism be a parent.
Genotype browser: 5 of the 9 genes have no marked variant site, so their site matrix is empty and says so. The non-coding signal per branch in progression.json is not drawn at all.
Compare: panel E (TFF) renders small because its 3.27 SL wingspan sets the shared camera distance; a per-panel fit would read better without losing the relative sizes.
The designs are in the species menu but Growth, Physiology and the gene lens treat them as the flying fish's geometry with no gene map of their own; nothing is asserted, but nothing is added either.
Sequences: genome-regions.json and engineered-diff.json are present but keyed by topic, not as rows; their tabs are empty and say so. The Genotype browser reads engineered-diff.json's headline only.

Sequences: the marked variant sites now carry alignment_column_1based and per-species residues; only the column and the label are drawn. The per-species residue windows would make the lat4a F326L site readable at a glance.

Genotype panel: only one of the 12 calibrated knobs (gja1b, adult) has both an adult regime and a Studio parameter to move. The other eleven measure a cleithrum length, a fin fold size, an endoskeletal disk, a hypural count or a transcript level, none of which this Studio has a parameter for. Adding those parameters (or saying so once, rather than per row) is the next step.

Genotype panel: the three magnitude-to-parameter mappings are written out in the page (KNOB_MODEL) with the clause each comes from. They belong in genotype/interventions.json as an explicit model_parameter field, so the page stops deciding which parameter a magnitude moves.
Genotype panel: the pathway slice covers 41 of the 44 genes the viewer can ask about; 3 have no row in pathways.slim.json and the panel says so per gene.
Growth could show the same Genotype panel: it already applies a knob inside its measured window, but it has no annotations and no picker.

Species switch: the gene lens, the organ menu and the drill-down still index the flying-fish blueprint, so with a zebrafish selected they only reach the 41 (adult) / 16 (larva) pieces that resolve by Uberon xref. A zebrafish-side index (ZFA, or the fin subtree widened to the whole body) would reach the rest.

Physiology on a zebrafish places physiology/circulation.json's generic teleost stations on the zebrafish pieces and says so, but the proxy vessel positions (dorsal aorta, cardinal vein) are still chosen against the flying-fish body and sit oddly on the larva; recompute them from the selected model's bounding box.

Design Studio with a zebrafish selected shows the flying fish's parameters and verdicts without applying them. A zebrafish baseline (SL, mass, fin ratio) would let the Studio check a zebrafish design, but no sourced zebrafish pectoral/SL exists, so C9 would be cannot-evaluate for every edit.
Compare: panel B still cannot show the winged-zebrafish phenotype, because the paper gives no magnitude; if a digitised fin length ever lands, scale B's fins and say where the number came from.
Growth draws the flying-fish clock only; a zebrafish growth view on development/zebrafish/trajectory.mjs with the larva-to-adult model swap would reuse what Compare now does.
Sequences: switch from the stand-in layout to sequences/ when it lands (check the alignment shape against seq.js normalise, the lat4a F326L site, the bird note)
Compare and Growth: hide or fade the 3D labels when the fish is tiny (the Compare camera now pulls in, Growth does not)
Physiology: the default camera framing at peel 3 leaves the fish off-centre (pre-existing); refit to the organs
Interactions: the tissue graph is crowded at phone width; consider a list view under 560 px
